&nbsp;

::: {.alert .alert-info}

The [dynaSpec](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/) package creates dynamic
spectrograms: spectrograms that move along with the sound. They can be shown as
interactive web pages or saved as videos. This vignette shows the basic usage of
all features. The article
[Customizing dynamic spectrograms](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/articles/customizing.html)
on the package website shows how to customize them. For detailed information on
each function, please refer to the
[function reference](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/index.html)
or use the help files within R (e.g., `?dynaspec`).

:::

# Installation

Install the latest development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("maRce10/dynaSpec")

#load package
library(dynaSpec)
```

Web pages do not need any external software. To create videos dynaSpec uses
[ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html), which must be installed and
available in the system path (see the installation instructions in the
[README](https://github.com/maRce10/dynaSpec#ffmpeg)).

# Layers

Dynamic spectrograms are built in layers, as 'ggplot2' graphs: `dynaspec()` takes the sound, and layers are added with `+`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
dynaspec(wave, flim = c(1, 10)) +          # the sound (and frequency and time ranges)
  spectrogram(wl = 300) +                   # panels: spectrogram, oscillogram, envelope, spectrum
  oscillogram() +
  selections(st) +                          # highlight parts of the sound
  captions("song", start = 0, end = 2) +    # text shown during a time range
  dynatheme(xlab = "Time (s)") +            # axis titles, text and colors
  player(speeds = c(1, 0.5)) +              # playback buttons of web pages
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7)                # style: static() (default), scrolling() or paged()
```

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| `spectrogram()` | Adds a spectrogram (window length, palette, amplitude range, ...) |
| `oscillogram()`, `envelope()` | Add an oscillogram or an amplitude envelope (above or below the spectrogram) |
| `spectrum()` | Adds a power spectrum next to the spectrogram |
| `overview()` | Adds a lower panel with the whole sound to scrolling spectrograms |
| `selections()` | Highlights parts of the sound with translucent boxes (e.g. from a selection table) |
| `captions()` | Text at a fixed position shown during a time range, like subtitles |
| `dynatheme()`, `dynatheme_dark()`, ... | Axis titles, fonts, colors of the figure and plot, and preset themes |
| `player()` | Playback controls of web pages (speed slider, loop, volume, download, ...) |
| `static()`, `scrolling()`, `paged()` | Style of the dynamic spectrogram |

Printing a `dynaspec` object shows an interactive web page: press play to watch the spectrogram along with the sound, click on it to play from that point, and use the speed slider to slow the sound down. In the R console web pages are shown in the RStudio viewer (or the web browser), and in R Markdown and Quarto documents (like this vignette) they are embedded in the document. `save_dynaspec()` saves them as web pages, videos or images (see [Saving](#saving-web-pages-videos-and-images)).

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(dynaSpec)
```

The examples use the canyon wren song and the barn swallow recordings included in the package. Sounds can be 'Wave' objects or '.wav' and '.mp3' files.

# Panels

Only the panels added as layers are shown. A spectrogram:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
data("canyon_wren")

wren <- dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300)

wren
```

Layers can be stored in an object (as `wren` above) and added later. A spectrogram with an oscillogram below it:

```{r}
wren + oscillogram()
```

Oscillograms and amplitude envelopes can go above or below the spectrogram, and a power spectrum can be added on its left or right side:

```{r}
wren +
  oscillogram(position = "above") +
  envelope() +
  spectrum(side = "right")
```

Without `spectrogram()` only the other panels are shown (e.g. only the oscillogram), and `dynaspec()` alone shows an empty panel with a time axis and the play line:

```{r}
dynaspec(canyon_wren) + oscillogram()
```

`flim` sets the frequency range (in kHz) and `crop` the part of the sound used (in s):

```{r}
dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10), crop = c(1, 3)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300)
```

# Styles

## Static spectrograms

The default style: a line moves over the whole figure as the sound plays. Long sounds can be split in several rows (`rows`; `height` sets the height of each row), and `play.line = FALSE` hides the moving line:

```{r}
wren + static(rows = 2, height = 350)
```

## Scrolling spectrograms

The spectrogram scrolls along a fixed play line, as in the Macaulay Library. `t.display` sets the time window (in s) shown at once, and `overview()` adds a lower panel with the whole sound, in which the part being shown is highlighted:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 9)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300) +
  overview() +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7)
```

Scrolling spectrograms show a single lower panel: an overview, an oscillogram or an envelope.

## Paged spectrograms

The spectrogram is split into pages (`t.display` sets the duration of each page), and a translucent box reveals the part of each page being played, as in Adobe Audition's spectral view. Pages turn as the sound plays:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# example WAV files included with dynaSpec
f <- list.files(system.file(package = "dynaSpec"), pattern = "\\.wav$", full.names = TRUE)

dynaspec(f[2]) +
  spectrogram() +
  paged(t.display = 2)
```

Settings not supplied take the defaults of each style. For instance, paged spectrograms use the 'inferno' palette and no axes by default.

# Playback

The speed slider slows the sound down. Slowing down also lowers the pitch (as when slowing down a tape), which makes fast features such as pulses easier to hear. The *keep pitch* button switches to slowing down while keeping the original pitch. `player()` sets the speeds offered (the first one is the initial speed) and whether the pitch is kept by default:

```{r}
wren + player(speeds = c(0.5, 1, 0.25), keep.pitch = TRUE)
```

`buttons` adds more controls: a time readout (shown by default), a loop button, a volume control, a button to download the sound and a full screen button:

```{r}
wren + player(buttons = c("time", "loop", "volume", "download", "fullscreen"))
```

Several players can be included in the same document or web page; only one sound plays at a time.

# Highlighting and labeling sounds

`selections()` highlights parts of the sound with translucent boxes. It takes a data frame with the start and end of each selection (in s), as the selection tables of [warbleR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=warbleR) and [ohun](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ohun). If it has 'bottom.freq' and 'top.freq' columns (in kHz) the boxes only span that frequency range, and colors and labels can be taken from its columns. With tables of several sound files (column 'sound.files') only the selections of the sound shown are used.

`captions()` adds text at a fixed position of the figure, shown (and optionally fading in and out) during a time range, like subtitles:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
st <- data.frame(
  start = c(0.4, 3.6),
  end = c(1.5, 4.8),
  bottom.freq = c(2, 1.5),
  top.freq = c(9, 5),
  labels = c("first notes", "last notes"),
  colors = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")
)

wren +
  selections(st, col = "colors", labels = "labels") +
  captions("Canyon wren", start = 0, end = 5.3, x = 0.85, y = 0.92, font = 3, fading = 0.3)
```

Both work in the three styles.

# Themes

`dynatheme()` sets the look of the figure in the same way for all styles: axis titles, text sizes and fonts, colors of axes and text, boxes, grid lines, backgrounds, the colors of the plot (e.g. the spectrogram palette, used when not supplied in `spectrogram()`) and the colors of the player controls:

```{r}
dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300, pal = viridis::mako, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1)) +
  dynatheme(xlab = "Tiempo (s)", ylab = "Frecuencia (kHz)", cex.lab = 1.3, font.lab = 2)
```

Preset themes set several settings at once: `dynatheme_dark()`, `dynatheme_presentation()`, `dynatheme_paper()`, `dynatheme_minimal()`, `dynatheme_transparent()` and `dynatheme_void()`. Their settings can be changed in the call:

```{r}
wren + oscillogram() + dynatheme_dark(cex.lab = 1.3)
```

# Saving web pages, videos and images

`save_dynaspec()` saves `dynaspec` objects. The extension of the file sets the output:

* `.html`: interactive web page, which can be shared as a single file or pasted into any web page
* `.mp4`: video, with the same settings. Videos can be used where web pages cannot, such as presentation slides (e.g. PowerPoint) or social media. [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) must be installed to create videos (see the installation instructions in the [README](https://github.com/maRce10/dynaSpec#installation))
* `.png`: still image of static spectrograms, or one image per page of paged spectrograms

```{r, eval = FALSE}
save_dynaspec(wren, "canyon_wren.html")
save_dynaspec(wren, "canyon_wren.png")
save_dynaspec(wren, "canyon_wren_static.mp4")
save_dynaspec(wren + scrolling(t.display = 1.7), "canyon_wren_scrolling.mp4")
```

Videos of static and paged spectrograms are created in a few seconds. Videos of scrolling spectrograms take longer, as every frame is rendered (a progress bar shows the progress).

Note that embedding sounds makes web pages larger (about 1.4 times the size of the sound file), so cut (e.g. with `crop`) or downsample long recordings before creating web pages.
